verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: the patch fixes defects in an existing psql mode, and two reviewers reproduced them. Two fixable points remain. standards-compat-2 asks which of the reviewer's fixes go to stable branches, since 0002 changes what EOF does at the prompt. standards-compat-1 asks what psql prints and returns with non-tty stdin. Neither would stop a committer from reading further.

brief.title: Fix Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D and input handling in psql single-step mode
brief.problem: psql single-step mode (SINGLESTEP, --single-step) misbehaves at its confirmation prompt. Ctrl-C does not leave the prompt, Ctrl-D runs all later queries (even in later \i scripts), any input other than "x" runs the query, and piped stdin answers its own prompts. The users are those who run scripts step by step to check each query.
brief.proposed_design: The confirmation prompt reads a full line with gets_interactive() (tab completion off), asks again on unknown input, and exits at once on Ctrl-C. Ctrl-D cancels only the current script, and nothing runs in single-step mode when stdin is not a tty. A reviewer added fixes for master: a per-call sigjmp_buf with a global pointer, and a Ctrl-D fix that stops later backslash commands on the same line.
user_visible_surface: Single-step prompt: input other than empty line or "x" now repeats the prompt instead of running the query.
Single-step prompt: Ctrl-C cancels immediately; Ctrl-D cancels the current script without affecting later \i scripts.
--single-step / SINGLESTEP with non-tty stdin no longer executes anything.
Ctrl-D at the prompt no longer runs later backslash commands on the same line, and no longer exits psql without readline (reviewer's 0002).
author_claims: The old behaviour surprises users, and most would expect Ctrl-C to leave the prompt.
Running the query on unrecognized input is a dangerous default for a mode meant for careful checking.
Single-step mode on non-tty stdin makes no sense; -f scripts still work.
The reviewer claims nested MainLoop() reuse of sigint_interrupt_jmp crashes psql on Ctrl-C at \prompt, back to 8.3.
brief.thread_state: Jelte Fennema-Nio liked the patch and asked for a distinct re-prompt naming the bad input. Rui Zhao found a Ctrl-C crash in the patch and Ctrl-D gaps, posted fixes 0001-0003, and began discussing backpatching; the message is truncated and Heikki has not replied.
unclear: Whether Heikki accepts the reviewer's 0001 and 0002 and the split into master fixes plus feature patch.
Which fixes are proposed for backpatch; the reviewer's message is cut off there.
Whether Jelte's distinct re-prompt text was adopted.
The patch touches no documentation, so the psql docs may not describe the new prompt, Ctrl-D, or non-tty behaviour.
What psql prints or does when single-step mode is used with non-tty stdin.

objections.title: Backpatching the Ctrl-D fix changes stable-branch behaviour at EOF
objections.failure_scenario: A user on a stable branch drives single-step mode from a pipe or an expect script that ends with EOF, so all queries run. After a minor update with 0002, EOF cancels the script and skips later backslash commands. Their job now stops partway, and they learn this from missing results after the update.
objections.argument: Message #3 frames 0002 as a fix for master, then starts to discuss backpatching 0001 and 0002, and the message is cut off there. The SIGINT crash fix in 0001 is a clear bug fix. 0002 changes what EOF means at the prompt, and that behaviour has existed in every client back to at least 13. A committer would likely ask that only the crash fix go to stable branches.
objections.author_must_show: Which of 0001 and 0002 is proposed for stable branches, and why is the change in EOF behaviour acceptable in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 starts to discuss backpatching 0001 and 0002 and is cut off, so the visible thread does not answer the question. 0002 changes what EOF does at the prompt on every client from 13, which a committer would likely ask about before a minor release.

objections.title: Single-step with non-tty stdin silently changes from running to running nothing
objections.failure_scenario: A cron job runs `psql --single-step -f load.sql < /dev/null`, or pipes a script into psql with SINGLESTEP set in a shared psqlrc. Before the change, EOF at the prompt made every query run. After the upgrade nothing runs, and if psql exits 0 with no error, the operator finds out only when the data is missing.
objections.argument: Point 5 of the commit message turns an existing working, if odd, invocation into a no-op. The proposal does not say whether psql reports an error, prints a warning, or what exit status it returns. It also touches no documentation, so the --single-step entry would not describe the new rule. psql normally handles unusable option combinations by refusing loudly at startup, and a silent skip departs from that.
objections.author_must_show: With --single-step and non-tty stdin, what does psql print and what exit status does it return, and where is this documented?

critic.reasoning: The commit message says nothing runs with non-tty stdin, but not what psql prints or which exit status it returns, and the patch touches no documentation. The `-f` example is doubtful because the commit message says `-f` still works, but the piped case stands.

refuted.title: New sigjmp_buf pointer convention must be kept by every later psql prompt
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds an interactive read in psql, for example a new confirmation prompt, and calls sigsetjmp without saving and restoring the global pointer. Tests pass because nobody presses Ctrl-C at that point. A user who presses Ctrl-C there in a nested \i script gets a longjmp into a returned frame and a crash.
refuted.argument: Message #3 replaces the single global sigint_interrupt_jmp with local buffers and a global pointer that each site saves, sets and restores by hand, in MainLoop(), handleCopyIn(), the simple_prompt_extended() callers and singlestep_verify(). The bug it fixes went unnoticed since 8.3, which shows how quietly a mistake in this pattern hides. The prose does not mention a macro, an assertion, or a test that would fail when a new site skips the restore. The design is sound, but it moves the invariant into a hand-written convention.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the save, set and restore step be wrapped in one macro or helper, with an assertion or test that fails when a new sigsetjmp site in psql bypasses it?

critic.reasoning: The scenario already exists on master in a wider form: any nested sigsetjmp on the shared global buffer leaves a stale context. 0001 narrows it and follows the PG_TRY pattern, and asking for a macro is a code-structure point, which is out of scope.

precedents_retrieved.title: session username in default psql prompt
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal prepends the session user name (%n@) to the default psql PROMPT1, and maybe PROMPT2, so users can see which role they are connected as. Kori Lane posted a patch, and Andrew Dunstan later suggested replacing the database name with %~ to keep the prompt short.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected that the prompt repeats the name when the user and database names match. Tom Lane added that %~ does not shorten the prompt when they differ, and that the prompt would about double in length, which costs scarce prompt space. Andrew Dunstan withdrew the proposal because of this opposition.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: On the whole, I think we'd get more complaints about the default prompt having more-or-less doubled in length than we'd get kudos about this being a great usability improvement.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PATCH v2] Time option added to psql prompt (%T)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Daniel Gustafsson, Tom Lane, Greg Stark
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a %T escape to the psql prompt that prints the client's local time as HH24:MI:SS, with no format options. The aim was to see when each command ran without the shell backquote workaround, which behaves differently on Linux and Windows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The posted patch failed the CI build, and it still did not build at the end of the March commitfest, so it was returned with feedback. Tom Lane objected to using a scarce prompt escape for a niche need that %`date` already covers. Greg Stark and Tom Lane also argued that a single fixed time format would not satisfy users, and that command tags may be a better place for timestamps than the prompt.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This patch spent the March commitfest not building and still doesn't build, so I'm marking this returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new protocol message to make GUC_REPORT configurable and use it for psql prompt substitution of %N with the current user
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a psql prompt escape %N that shows the current role. To keep the prompt current, it adds a new protocol message and libpq functions (PQlinkParameterStatus, PQunlinkParameterStatus) that turn GUC_REPORT on or off for a given setting during a session.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch and said he would resend it once Jelte Fennema-Nio's _pq_.report_parameters patch is committed. Peter Eisentraut suggested a GUC that lists the settings to report instead of a new protocol message. Jelte Fennema-Nio argued that proxies such as PgBouncer already re-sync GUCs, so a GUC-based design is less fragile for them than a new message type with its own connection state.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think this is probably one of the core reasons why I would very much prefer GUCs over new message types to configure protocol extensions like this: It means proxies would not to keep track of and re-sync a new kind of connection state every time a protocol extension is added.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add %r substitution for psql prompts to show recovery status
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Tatsuo Ishii, Alexander Korotkov, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a %r substitution to psql prompts that displays "&" when the connected server is in recovery (i.e. a standby). The patch determined this by sending a pg_is_in_recovery() query to the server each time the prompt substitution is evaluated.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected to issuing an extra query every time the prompt is drawn, and asked how this would behave inside an aborted transaction. Several reviewers said the backend should instead report recovery status to the client through a parameter status message, possibly by reporting transaction_read_only. The entry was returned with feedback because this would be a much bigger change than the initial patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm setting this CF item to returned with feedback, since it would
apparently be a much bigger change than then initial patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: New psql prompt substitution %r (m = master, r = replica)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane, David Fetter, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a new %r substitution to psql's prompt that shows whether the connected server is a master (m) or a replica (r). The patch added a new server GUC (is_master), reported to the client, to supply this status.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that a binary master/replica flag does not fit upcoming replication variants such as logical replication. They also noted that the status is only checked at connect time and so becomes wrong if the server is promoted during the session, and that a new GUC is not a suitable approach for this. The author then concluded that no patch was needed, since the same result can be had with \gset and a psqlrc setup.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also, the patch as given is broken since it fails to account for the
server being promoted while a psql session is open.

precedents_retrieved.title: Refactoring of connection with password prompt loop for frontends
precedents_retrieved.summary: Consolidate the repeated frontend pattern of connecting to the backend with a password-prompt retry loop (used in several client tools) into a single shared routine in src/fe_utils. The patch unified error handling across tools but left out pg_dumpall and the code paths that prompt for a password before the first connection attempt.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author marked it returned with feedback himself. Open design questions remained: an unresolved XXX comment, and the handling of tools (vacuumlo, scripts/common.c, pg_dump) that prompt for a password before the first connection or reuse it across connections. Resolving these needed further work to avoid password exposure hazards. The patch also drew little review attention.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For now I am switching the patch as returned with feedback as there is
much more to consider.  And it did not attract much attention either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restart pg_usleep when interrupted
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a sleep function, later named pg_usleep_non_interruptible, that restarts nanosleep() with the remaining time when a signal interrupts it, and stops once the requested time has passed. Vacuum cost delay would use it so the parallel vacuum leader sleeps the full delay even when parallel workers send it frequent progress messages.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after the thread questioned whether the extra code was worth it. Nathan Bossart noted that interrupts rarely hit a vacuum delay point and that rate-limiting worker progress reports to 1 Hz would remove most of them, and the uninterruptible sleep would make vacuum slower to react to SIGTERM or cancel. CF #5118 would also change how pg_usleep() handles these interrupts, so the author left the question to that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Is it really that important to delay with that level of accuracy?

precedents_retrieved.title: Trigger failsafe when VACUUM is run in single user mode
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a VACUUM option for single-user mode, first called VACUUM LIMIT and later VACUUM (EMERGENCY), that vacuums only tables whose xid or mxid age passes a fixed cutoff, with failsafe behavior and no index cleanup or truncation. The aim is to get out of single-user mode quickly after a wraparound shutdown.
precedents_retrieved.objection: During review, the thread found that the v14 failsafe already turns off heap truncation, so plain VACUUM should work under the postmaster at xidStopLimit. The plan then moved to removing the advice to use single-user mode. Noah Misch then showed that VACUUM can still create multixacts at multiStopLimit, so more work was needed. The author was away sick and withdrew the work for v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I gather from subsequent discussion that a full solution goes beyond just a new warning message and documentation. Either way I'm not quite prepared to address this in time for v15.

precedents_retrieved.title: Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
Reverted commit(s): Read extension script files in text not binary mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert commit 924e03917 in favor of adding code to convert \r\n to \n
explicitly, on Windows only.  The idea of letting text mode do the
work fails for a couple of reasons:

* Per Microsoft documentation, text mode also causes control-Z to be
interpreted as end-of-file.  While it may be unlikely that extension
scripts contain control-Z, we've historically allowed it, and breaking
the case doesn't seem wise.

* Apparently, on some Windows configurations, "r" mode is interpreted
as binary not text mode.  We could force it with "rt" but that would
be inconsistent with our code elsewhere, and it would still require
Windows-specific coding.

Thanks to Alexander Lakhin for investigation.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The only listed row, [P13], is about stopping psql command execution after a connection reset, with no recorded reason; it shares only the psql area. Message #1 points to an earlier thread about PQcancel, but only as the place where the single-step complaint was first mentioned, not as a prior attempt at this fix.
The interactive prompt changes (re-prompt on unknown input, Ctrl-C exits at once) add no syntax, GUC or dump surface, and I raise no objection to them.

The proposal changes only psql client-side input handling: the single-step prompt, SIGINT jump buffers and EOF handling. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or server ABI. The gets_interactive() signature change is internal to psql and does not affect extensions.

The proposal changes only client-side psql behaviour at the single-step prompt. It adds no privilege, role, server code path or monitoring exposure, and it gives no user access to data or sessions they lack today. Each change makes the default safer: unknown input no longer runs the query, Ctrl-D no longer runs later commands, and non-tty stdin runs nothing. The Ctrl-C crash in message #3 is a local client abort with no cross-user effect, so it belongs to the correctness angle. Without the code, I could not check whether the sigjmp_buf pointer changes leave a stale pointer on any error path.

From the maintenance angle the proposal fits core: psql behaviour, no hot path, no new dependency, and a committer wrote it, with a reviewer who split it into fixes for master first. The one concern is the hand-kept sigjmp_buf pointer convention.

This is a bug fix to psql's existing single-step mode, and it adds no new mechanism. No core feature, option, extension or external tool gives a working Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D or strict input handling at that prompt, so this angle raises nothing. The listed precedent [P13] covers connection reset, an unrelated topic.

No demand objection. The patch fixes defects in an existing documented mode: Ctrl-D runs later scripts unconfirmed, and nested Ctrl-C crashes psql in every client since 8.3, so it is not new surface needing users. Two other people tested it and reproduced the problems (messages #2, #3), and the cost falls on single-step users only.
